interpretation: Paired controls and the predefined first-expansion ramp use the same initial weights, examples, loss, AdamW configuration, and selection gates; moments persist within each fit. Gradient and update-magnitude changes are diagnostic; generated fidelity, count, EOS, and selected-versus-final quality are reported separately.
limitations: Previously exposed authored composition; no fresh holdout or natural-statute benchmark
Top-K events are selected exceptional updates, not representative gradients
Separate branch backward passes reconcile only within the recorded numerical tolerance
The ramp changes only the effective learning rate for the fixed first-expansion window; selection gates and optimizer moments persist
Per-step update magnitude is observed from parameter snapshots; sums of magnitudes are not net parameter displacement
Tracing and update observation add measured cost; smaller spikes do not imply better generated quality
Balanced count exposure also updates the shared source conditioner
Reconstruction and gradient replay confer no native family or Lake qualification
Historical 8D unchanged; no verified local768D input experiment
